symptom: No MDL way to add an operation to an existing consumed REST service: `alter consumed rest service M.S add operation X (…)` fails `no viable alternative at input 'alterconsumedrest'` (also `alter rest client`, `create operation … in`), and `create or modify` naming only the new operations deleted the stored ones with only `Modified rest client: M.S (2 operations)`
cause: Consumed REST services had CREATE [OR MODIFY] and DROP only, and their writer (UpdateConsumedRestService) rebuilds the whole document from the semantic model, so even a restatement of every operation resets what the reader does not carry
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_rest_clients_alter.go` (alterRestClient), `mdl/backend/modelsdk/consumed_rest_edit.go` (EditConsumedRestService — a raw splice via UpdateRawUnitPatch), grammar `alterConsumedRestServiceAction`; tests `mdl/executor/issue1608_consumed_rest_alter_test.go`
insight: An ALTER built as read-semantic → modify → UpdateX(model) is a whole-document rewrite in disguise: it resets every unmodelled property of every sibling, which is exactly the loss the report wanted to avoid (an operation made in Studio Pro). Build it as a splice of the stored bson.D instead — untouched list elements pass through as stored bytes, a modified element re-encodes only the keys the statement named (each taken from the CREATE encoder, so new and created elements stay identical), and save through UpdateRawUnitPatch. Prove it with a seed only Studio Pro writes (Rest$OptionalQueryParameterUsage plus a TestValue on a query parameter): byte-compare the sibling before/after, and keep the control — a CREATE OR MODIFY from describe output resets the seed — or the seed may be one no rewrite can lose. A temporary swap of the splice for UpdateConsumedRestService failed both 'left as stored' tests. `mx check` on the result needs its own control too: a copy with one operation's Accept header removed reports CE7062, so a clean check of the real output means something
